title: SlimIO: Lightweight I/O Path Design for Write Isolation in FDP-backed In-Memory Databases
problem: In-Memory Databases (IMDBs) using snapshot-based persistence suffer from syscall overhead, inter-process I/O contention, and SSD garbage collection delays that degrade performance
motivation: With growing HPC data management needs, minimizing I/O latency and reducing SSD wear (write amplification) are critical for database performance and hardware longevity in large-scale systems
method: SlimIO avoids expensive system call overhead by writing directly to storage hardware (passthru I/O). It uses Flexible Data Placement (FDP) SSDs, which allow the database to control exactly which regions of flash storage receive writes, rather than letting the SSD firmware decide. By isolating each process's writes, it prevents different processes' write patterns from creating performance interference through the SSD's garbage collection and wear-leveling.
key_novelty: SlimIO controls database writes directly to Flexible Data Placement SSDs with process isolation and passthru I/O, ensuring each database write maps to exactly one SSD write and achieving a write amplification factor of 1.0.
contributions: I/O passthru mechanism reducing syscall overhead
FDP-based write isolation preventing garbage collection interference
50% latency reduction (99.9%-ile) and 30% query throughput improvement
Write amplification factor of 1.00 (zero redundant writes)
limitations: FDP SSD availability limited; syscall reduction benefit depends on I/O-intensive workloads; evaluation limited to Redis
